_about: Utah lawn-conversion incentives. One saved table, not live lookups. Rates in USD per sq ft of lawn removed; 'estimated up to' uses rate_high. Verified 2026-10-27 against the provider detail pages on utahwatersavers.com and slowtheflow.org (quoted in each row's source). City-to-provider mapping follows the portal's eligibility list (https://www.utahwatersavers.com/program-eligibility-page): a listed city has a qualifying landscape ordinance; an unlisted city is ineligible. Cities not mapped below fall back to the statewide row, which may be wrong for them. None of the program pages give a separate park strip rate.

statewide_rules.program: Utah Water Savers Landscape Incentive Program (Utah Division of Water Resources + local providers)
statewide_rules.virtual_inspection_allowed: Utah Admin Code R653-11-7 allows completion inspections to be physical or virtual; the Division's own track uses a virtual pre-conversion visit
disqualifiers: Removing or killing lawn before the site visit and approval
Lawn not living and maintained at the site visit
Account not in good standing with water provider
City without a qualifying water-efficient landscape ordinance (not on the eligibility list)
Artificial turf, concrete, or non-drip irrigation in the converted area
Remaining lawn strips narrower than 8 ft (CUWCD)
Project not finished within 12 months of approval
statewide_rules.legal: Utah Code 73-10-34 (2022 H.B. 121 turf removal incentive); Utah Admin Code R653-11

providers.name: Central Utah Water Conservancy District (standard program)
providers.notes: Sandy and Salt Lake City customers apply through the state portal and are routed to CUWCD's standard program (SLC has no separate per-sq-ft program; its FAQ points to utahwatersavers.com). Switch-to-drip is $1.00/sq ft; trees $50 each up to 10.
providers.source: https://www.utahwatersavers.com/cuwcd-landscape-incentive-program-details ('Incentive Amount = $3.00/square foot'; 'The maximum incentive amount allowed per property is $50,000'); https://www.slc.gov/utilities/conservation/water-conservation-faq/

providers.name: Central Utah Water Conservancy District (rural program)
Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District (member cities)
providers.notes: Initial site visit must be approved before any lawn is removed. Park strips must meet planting bed requirements. No cap stated on the program page.
providers.source: https://slowtheflow.org/rebates/jordan-valley/ ('Incentive Amount = $3.00 per sq ft'; 'A minimum project area of 200 sq ft is required')

providers.name: Utah Division of Water Resources statewide track
providers.notes: For eligible cities with no local program (e.g. Cedar City, Moab, Tooele). Pre-conversion site visit is virtual; 365 days to finish; private wells not eligible. The 200 sq ft minimum can be waived when all lawn is removed from a park strip.
providers.source: https://www.utahwatersavers.com/division-of-water-resources-landscape-incentive-program-details ('Incentives are for $2.00 per square foot of grass removed... (maximum incentive amount of $50,000/application)')
